stories.event: SpaceX targets Starship Flight 15 (Booster 22, Ship 42) from Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas, on Friday 13 November 2026 in a 75-minute window opening 4:45 p.m. CST (22:45 UTC), pending FAA approval; the licence was still outstanding on 10–11 November. It is the first attempt to catch both stages with the launch tower: the booster about 6.5 minutes after liftoff, the ship about 22.5 hours later (around 3:17 p.m. CST Saturday for an on-time launch) after about 14 orbits at ~275 km and deployment of 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The ship returns only if its systems are healthy. SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on Flights 5, 7 and 8 but never a ship; Flight 14 on 28 September was the first orbital flight. V3 boosters were lost after engine relight failures on Flights 12 and 13 (SpaceX via Space.com, Starlust, The Space Road, Teslarati, Wikipedia).

stories.event: The UN climate conference COP31 runs 9–20 November 2026 in Antalya, Turkey, with Turkey's Murat Kurum as COP President and Australia's Chris Bowen as 'President of Negotiations' (ENB). The two subsidiary bodies, SBSTA 65 and SBI 65, are officially scheduled for 9–14 November (UNFCCC agendas FCCC/SBI/2026/18, FCCC/SBSTA/2026/7) and must close on Saturday 14 November, forwarding draft texts to ministers for week two; the presidency will set second-week working modalities after the SB closing plenaries. Agenda fights were averted only by pre-sessional consultations running into the early hours of 9 November, logistics problems delayed sessions, and positions on the adaptation goal, the mitigation work programme and the just transition mechanism remain far apart (ENB). The presidency, which plans a 'Presidency-initiated, Party-driven' cover decision, takes written inputs on it until Saturday. In the last five COPs the SBs closed before midnight on their scheduled day three times (COP27, COP28, COP30) and ran past midnight twice (COP26, COP29), several times by under an hour (ENB).

stories.event: Melaka (Malacca) holds its 16th state election on Saturday 14 November 2026: 28 seats, 15 for a majority, 687,697 voters, 79 candidates (Election Commission via Malay Mail, The Star). Barisan Nasional (UMNO-led) runs 23 candidates and its partner Perikatan Nasional 5 (two of them PAS) in a seat pact; Pakatan Harapan runs 24, Bersatu 7 separately and Rafizi Ramli's Bersama 16. In 2021 BN won 21 seats, PH 5 and PN 2 (both Bersatu). PH left the BN-led state government in July 2026 over an amendment creating seven appointed seats. In neighbouring Negeri Sembilan on 1 August a BN–PN pact won 25 of 36 seats and PH fell from 17 to 11. BN leaders target 25–26 seats; PH defends Bukit Katil, Ayer Keroh, Bandar Hilir, Kesidang and Kota Laksamana. Ilham Centre says about 13% of voters were undecided; no numeric surveys have been published (The Vibes, NST, Wikipedia).
